places.name: Cihangir
tips: Most of the places in this guide are in Cihangir or the wider Beyoğlu area.
places.background: A leafy, café-heavy residential quarter and the base for most places in this guide. It sits on a hillside in Beyoğlu between Taksim/Sıraselviler and the Bosphorus shore at Fındıklı, and is known for its bohemian, artsy reputation, its cafés and its street cats. Cihangir Mosque stands at its lower end.

photos.credit: Photo: Grzegorz Jereczek from Gdańsk, Poland · CC BY-SA 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Doğacıyız Gourmet
places.pp: ₺725 (set breakfast) plus drinks; à la carte menemen ₺220–300
tips: Eastern cuisine, more touristy.
places.background: A Hatay-flavoured breakfast house in Cihangir, different from the usual Turkish kahvaltı and more geared to visitors. It is known for the serpme Antakya breakfast (biberli ekmek, tuzlu yoğurt, zahter, muhammara, sürk), muhlama and Hatay-style gözleme. By its own account it has been running for about 14 years, and Yemek.com says its produce comes from its own land and is sold by the jar.
places.address: Kılıçali Paşa, Akarsu Yokuşu Sk. No:41A, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Ağa Bilardo Cafe (the menemen billiard hall)
tips: The best menemen, in a weird place: a billiard hall in Cihangir.
Perfect for two: share a menemen with cheese and a gözleme with cheese, with tea.
places.background: An old-school Cihangir billiard hall and kahvehane where locals play billiards, okey and tavla over cheap, always-fresh tea. Reviewers praise the tost, served with pickles on the side. One reviewer called it perhaps the only billiard hall you can come to with family.
places.address: Firuzağa, Taktaki Yokuşu No:2/A (off Sıraselviler Cd.), Cihangir, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Van Kahvaltı Evi
tips: Favourite #2. Simple, less sophisticated, but everything you get is delicious.
places.background: A hugely popular Cihangir institution serving Van-style (eastern Anatolian) breakfast: murtuğa, kavut, otlu peynir, çemen, pişi, gözleme and fresh pomegranate juice. It is famous for its weekend queue; weekdays are calmer. There is a sister branch in Nişantaşı (Valikonağı Cad., Sezai Selek Sk. 19).
places.address: Kılıçali Paşa / Firuzağa, Defterdar Yokuşu No:52/A, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Kahve 6
tips: Favourite #1. Gourmet, curated ingredients, back garden.
Try the İzmir breakfast, the goat cheese omelette and the lor peynirli gözleme.
places.background: A cosy, long-standing Cihangir breakfast café with a green back garden with a pool, serving breakfast and home cooking. Highlights include the 'Dolu Dolu' breakfast, the İzmir breakfast (sahanda Bergama tulum, Tire karadut, lor), the aubergine börek, the lor gözleme and the house granola. Time Out was already reviewing it in 2011.
places.address: Kılıçali Paşa Mah., Akarsu Cad., Anahtar Sk. No:13/A, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Cihangir Çiğ Köfte
tips: Get the çiğ köfte dürüm.
places.background: A hole-in-the-wall takeaway on Turnacıbaşı Caddesi selling çiğ köfte, the meatless bulgur-and-pepper-paste version, in dürüm or by the portion. A cheap vegan snack.
places.address: Turnacıbaşı Cd. 61a, Katip Mustafa Çelebi, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Halil Usta Kebap & Lahmacun
tips: Get the Adana kebab dürüm, the lahmacun and the lentil soup.
places.background: A small, cheap kebab and lahmacun shop for a quick Adana dürüm, lahmacun or lentil soup. It is on Hocazade Sokak just off Sıraselviler Caddesi, between Taksim and Cihangir.
places.address: Katip Mustafa Çelebi Mah., Hocazade Sk. No:7/A (off Sıraselviler Cd.), 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Baran Lahmacun
tips: For Adana kebab, lahmacun, lentil soup and the tavuk (chicken) wrap.
places.background: A sit-down Diyarbakır-style stone-oven lahmacun and kebab restaurant on Turnacıbaşı Caddesi, between Galatasaray and Cihangir. The menu covers Diyarbakır and Antep lahmacun, pide, Adana and Urfa kebab, sac tava, lentil soup, dürüms including chicken şiş, and künefe, plus breakfast.
places.address: Kuloğlu Mah., Turnacıbaşı Cd. No:39/A, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Fıccın Lokanta Cihangir
tips: Andrés: definitely.
places.background: A Cihangir lokanta serving Circassian and home-style dishes: Circassian velibah (a gözleme-like pastry) and Circassian mantı alongside mücver, Kayseri yağlaması and zeytinyağlılar. It is the second branch of Fıccın on Kallavi Sokak in Asmalımescit, opened on Firuzağa Square in 2026.
places.address: Akarsu Yokuşu 44/A, Firuzağa, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Mayko Lokanta
places.background: A tiny, cosy Cihangir restaurant with a short menu of modern home-style Turkish dishes and meze, including dolma, eggplant balls, fava and many vegan options, which makes it good for mixed vegan and meat-eating groups. There are only a few tables, so book ahead. It is run by family and friends, and reviewers call it shabby-chic.
places.address: Kuloğlu Mah., Hacıoğlu Sk. No:1A, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Tomtom Kebap
places.background: A tiny kebab and dürüm shop on Yeni Çarşı Caddesi, very popular with tourists and often with a queue. It is known for Adana and Urfa kebab, lamb dürüm, hummus and lentil soup, with a few sidewalk tables. It is said to have been founded in 2018.
places.address: Firuzağa, Yeni Çarşı Cd. 39 A, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Limonlu Bahçe
tips: Turkish restaurant with very, very nice vibes in Cihangir, set in a garden that makes you forget the hustle and bustle of the city. My go-to place to bring people while it's still warm enough.
places.background: A leafy hidden garden for breakfast, a long lunch or evening drinks, more about the setting than the food. The 350 m² garden of lemon, magnolia, pine and linden trees, with resident tortoises, sits behind the French Consulate on Yeni Çarşı, and the Turkish–Mediterranean menu runs from breakfast to late drinks, with house lemonade and cocktails. It opened in June 2001, billed as Istanbul's first 'chill-out zone'.
places.address: Tomtom Mh., Yeni Çarşı Cd. No:74, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Journey
tips: Delicious food in a plant-filled space. Lots of freelancers work from here, especially on weekdays.
places.background: A laid-back, two-storey all-day café-restaurant on Akarsu Caddesi, with a work-friendly upstairs mezzanine whose communal table is popular with laptop workers. The food is Turkish-inspired with a European twist (such as honey-roasted lamb shank), plus brunch and cocktails; good, if a bit pricey. It has been a neighbourhood staple since at least 2010.
places.address: Kılıçali Paşa Mah., Akarsu Cd. (Akarsu Yokuşu) No:21/A, Cihangir, Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Susam Cafe
tips: Great place to work if you want good food too. Has outside and semi-outside tables, a few with plug sockets.
places.background: A relaxed, long-running all-day café on Susam Sokak with terrace tables, which stays open late as a bar. It serves breakfast, salads, burgers, wraps, pasta and flatbread pizza, and its signature drink is the 'Egeli Mojito' with black mulberry. Time Out was already reviewing it in 2011.
places.address: Kılıçali Paşa Mah., Susam Sk. No:11, Cihangir, Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Emily's Garden
tips: A gorgeous garden in the middle of Cihangir. Quite fancy at night, but in the daytime it's quiet and peaceful.
places.background: A hidden garden bistro on Susam Sokak: a calm daytime spot for work or brunch, and romantic dinners and drinks at night. A small café front leads to a bar, long tables and a tree-lit back garden, and the Mediterranean/Italian-leaning menu covers pasta, seafood, breakfast and brunch. It occupies the site of The White Mill, which moved to Akaretler, and has been around since at least 2019.
places.address: Pürtelaş Hasan Efendi Mah., Susam Sk. No:13, 34427 Cihangir, Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Kinu Matcha
tips: Kinu Matcha: serves Petra coffee.
places.background: A small matcha bar on Faik Paşa Caddesi, on the Cihangir–Çukurcuma edge, opened in early 2026. Besides matcha drinks it serves coffee made with Petra beans. Open Tuesday to Sunday, 09:00–20:00 (spring 2026 listing).
places.address: Kuloğlu, Faik Paşa Cd. No: 29/A, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Müz Botanik & Kahve
places.background: A small, plant-filled neighbourhood café on Hayriye Caddesi in Çukurcuma, for a coffee break. Time Out described it in 2016 as a place to sip Petra's coffee while feeling like you are in a tiny forest, and a good stop for reading.
places.address: Firuzağa, Hayriye Cd. 18/A, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Mellow
tips: My go-to place in Cihangir for a drink, and maybe a quick bite, with friends after work.
The Tinkerbell cocktail (passion fruit and kiwi) is delicious.
places.background: A two-floor tapas kitchen and bar on Akarsu Yokuşu, Cihangir's main bar street, for easy after-work drinks; the upstairs floor is the nicer one. It serves Turkish-fusion tapas and mezes with boutique Turkish wines and cocktails, and Time Out reviewed it in 2015.
places.address: Kılıçali Paşa Mah., Akarsu Yokuşu No:30/B, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Geyik
places.background: A tiny, crowded Cihangir bar, a brick-walled third-wave coffee roastery by day that turns into a busy cocktail bar at night, with regulars drinking on the pavement of Akarsu Yokuşu. It has been a Cihangir fixture since at least 2014.
places.address: Kılıçali Paşa Mah., Akarsu Yokuşu No:22/A, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Cafe 21 Cihangir
tips: The kitchen is open almost the whole night; it's the only place around like that.
places.background: A packed, long-running café-bar-restaurant on Coşkun Sokak off Akarsu Yokuşu, about ten steps from Geyik, where you can still eat at 2–3 am. It is popular with young locals, the veranda tables are hard to get, and the full food menu (mantı included) is served into the small hours.
places.address: Akarsu Yokuşu Cd., Coşkun Sk. No:2/1 (some listings: No:21), 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Zeytuna
tips: Alternative bar-restaurant: an expat hub, with blues nights, tango nights and more.
places.background: A restaurant, bar and events space on the first floor of the Cezayir building, mixing Lebanese, Syrian, Palestinian and Turkish cooking. The falafel is very good and there are many vegetarian options. It also runs a cultural programme of music nights.
places.address: Firuzağa, Hayriye Cd. No:12 (Cezayir building, 1st floor), 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Kaktüs Cihangir
places.background: A Cihangir institution with a winter garden: a café serving breakfast and brunch by day, and a bar and restaurant with cocktails and gastropub food at night, with a weekly Wednesday record night. It is an offshoot of the old Kaktüs off İstiklal, opened because many of its regulars had moved to Cihangir, and is one of the neighbourhood's most rooted venues.
places.address: Pürtelaş Hasan Efendi, Cihangir Cd. No:16/A, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Tavern
places.warning: Aug 2025 TripAdvisor review reports being charged the higher price for smaller cocktails plus a service fee; check the bill.
places.background: A small, busy cocktail bar on Hayriye Caddesi, a few doors from Zeytuna on the Cezayir/Firuzağa strip next to Cihangir. It serves creative signature cocktails to DJ sets and is pricier than average.
places.address: Firuzağa, Hayriye Cd. No:16/A, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Solera Winery
tips: A small bar with a huge variety of wines.
places.background: A cosy, crowded wine cave off İstiklal, lined floor-to-ceiling with bottles, with a huge choice of Turkish wines alongside imported ones. Bottles can be bought to take away at a discount, and the food (simple mezes, cheese and pasta) is secondary. It is a long-standing small shop and bar, and one of the pioneers of Istanbul's wine-bar scene.
places.address: Tomtom Mah., Yeni Çarşı Cd. No:44, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Ziba
places.background: An unpretentious, long-standing corner pub just off İstiklal near Galatasaray for casual drinks, with a crowd that routinely spills onto the street and the summer terrace. It serves draught and bottled beers, signature cocktails, burgers and snacks.
places.address: Tomtom, Akansu Sk. No:10, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: MiniMüzikhol
places.background: An intimate, sweaty underground room for house and minimal, and the late-night reference for Cihangir. The small, unsigned club (capacity 200) is on the ground floor of a Cihangir apartment block and has been running since around 2009–2010. It bills itself as the oldest underground club in Istanbul and has hosted DJs such as Ivan Smagghe, Acid Pauli and DJ Tennis.
places.address: Soğancı Sk. (Cihangir Palas) No:3/1, Cihangir, Beyoğlu/İstanbul

photos.credit: Photo: minimuzikhol.club

places.name: Kiki
places.background: A popular bar-club on Sıraselviler: dinner and cocktails early in the front restaurant-bar and garden, then house and tech-house dancing in the back room until morning, with long queues at weekends. It opened as a tea shop in Çukurcuma and moved here in 2008.
places.address: Sıraselviler Cd. No:42, Beyoğlu/İstanbul (opposite the German Hospital)

places.name: Roxy
places.background: A veteran Taksim club that now mostly hosts promoter nights (techno, hardcore, Latin) and concerts. Running since 1994 with founder Cem Selcen, it opened a new season on 26 September 2025, described by CNN Türk as 30 years at the heart of Istanbul nightlife. Its electronic arm operates as RX Istanbul.
places.address: Arslanyatağı Sk., Cihangir, Beyoğlu/İstanbul (corner of Sıraselviler Cd.; RA: No:5, Time Out: No:1/3)

places.name: Let's Relax Cihangir
tips: 45-minute massage: Thai, Thai with oil ('Thai for beginners') or a standard Swedish.
places.background: A clean, professional Thai-style massage studio, rated 5.0 from 112 reviews on Fresha. Thai therapists offer Thai, Thai-with-oil, Swedish, aromatherapy and deep-tissue massages, plus nails and waxing. It is the Cihangir branch of a small Istanbul chain (Taksim İstiklal, Cihangir, Beşiktaş, Nişantaşı), apparently unrelated to the Thai 'Let's Relax Spa' chain.
places.address: Kuloğlu Mah., Sıraselviler Cd., Mavi Plaza No:84 Kat:2, Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Ağa Hamamı
tips: Around 100 m down the road. Lovely, though a little more touristy. Most hamams are single-sex; Ağa Hamamı is mixed.
places.background: A small historic hamam. The traditional package is ₺3,600 by card or ₺3,100 cash (entry ₺1,800, kese scrub ₺900, foam wash ₺900), or ₺5,600 / ₺5,100 with a 20-minute oil massage; kese, soap, shampoo, peştemal, towel and slippers are provided. The hamam says Mehmed the Conqueror built it in 1454 as a hunting lodge with a bath below, renovated in 1844 under Abdülmecid, and markets itself as Istanbul's oldest Turkish bath.
places.address: Turnacıbaşı Sk., Kuloğlu, Beyoğlu/İstanbul (OSM: No:66; Time Out: No:48)

places.name: Galata
tips: Right next to Cihangir, only 15 min walk away. It has the famous Galata Tower (definitely worth going up for the incredible view), as well as a bunch of tasty restaurants, cafés and vintage shops.
places.background: A touristy but atmospheric hill around Galata Tower, good for wandering, food and shops. The historic Genoese-era quarter lies on the north side of the Golden Horn, centred on the 14th-century tower, with steep lanes of restaurants, cafés, music and vintage shops running down from Tünel and İstiklal towards Karaköy.

photos.credit: Photo: Juraj Patekar · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Alexxx Malev · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Lades Menemen
places.background: A small, no-frills Beyoğlu eatery on Sadri Alışık Sokak, off İstiklal, known for its menemen. Come for a pan of it.
places.address: Katip Mustafa Çelebi Mah., Sadri Alışık Sk. No:11/12, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Suat Usta Mersin Tantuni
places.background: A long-running, late-night Mersin tantuni counter in the back streets off İstiklal near Taksim, and the obvious replacement for the closed Emine Ana. It is a one-dish shop serving tantuni dürüm with Mersin şalgam and pickled peppers, where crowds from İstiklal and Nevizade end their night.
places.address: Katip Mustafa Çelebi Mah., Büyükparmakkapı Tel Sk. No:1 (Çukurlu Çeşme Sk. corner), 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Anas Chicken
tips: A chain with restaurants mostly in Syria and a few in Turkey; Syrian friends are obsessed with it. Get the fried chicken or a dürüm to go for an easy lunch.
places.background: Syrian fried chicken and shawarma, mainly takeaway: broasted chicken, chicken shawarma dürüm and kabsa. The chain (Anas Gıda Grubu) was founded in Damascus in 1991 and lists three active Istanbul branches: Beyoğlu (Taksim), a short walk from İstiklal, plus Aksaray and Kayaşehir.
places.address: Kuloğlu Mah., Sadri Alışık Sk. No:8, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Dürümzade
tips: Hole-in-the-wall for Hatay food, spicier than western Turkey's. Famous since Anthony Bourdain gave it his blessing. The best dürüm I've had in Turkey.
places.background: A tiny hole-in-the-wall charcoal dürüm shop a few minutes' walk from İstiklal Caddesi, serving lamb, Adana, chicken and liver dürüm. It became famous after Anthony Bourdain ate a lamb şiş dürüm there for the Istanbul episode of 'No Reservations', and has had a lot of tourist traffic since. The double-lamb 'duble kuzu dürüm' is the signature.
places.address: Hüseyinağa Mah., Kamer Hatun Cd. No:26/A (corner of Topçekenler Sk.), 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Asmalı Mescit Dürümcü
places.background: A small dürüm and kebab shop on Nergiz Sokak, open late, for a late-night stop among the meyhanes of the Asmalımescit bar district.
places.address: Şahkulu Mah., Nergiz Sk. No:2/A, 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Helvetia
places.background: A cheap, busy, no-frills lokanta by Tünel where you point to choose from seasonal, mostly vegetarian home-cooked dishes on the counter by the open kitchen, such as pazı borani, köfte, dolma and legumes; lunch is the peak, and there is no alcohol. It occupies a former beerhouse, and the old 'Helvetia' name painted on the wall is a remnant of the original building. Time Out once gave it its 'best home-cooked food' award.
places.address: Asmalı Mescit, General Yazgan Sk. No:8, 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Zübeyir Ocakbaşı
places.background: A classic, busy ocakbaşı over three floors in Taksim; sit at the grill counter and book ahead at weekends. It is known for Adana kebab, ribs (kaburga), liver, gavurdağı salad and quince dessert. Grill master Zübeyir opened it in 2006, and the family's start in the trade goes back to 1986 with brothers Hamit and Zübeyir.
places.address: Şehit Muhtar Mh., Bekar Sk. No:28, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Fıccın
tips: Outdoor restaurant just off İstiklal, on a little side street. Delicious Caucasian food with tasty wines.
Must-tries: the shredded Circassian chicken (çerkez tavuğu), the dumplings, and the meze starters, including aubergine in tomato sauce and beetroot with yoghurt.
places.background: Long-running, good-value Circassian home cooking on pedestrian Kallavi Sokak off İstiklal, with outdoor tables. Named after its signature Circassian meat pastry, it also serves çerkez tavuğu, Circassian mantı and olive-oil dishes, and unusually for a lokanta it serves alcohol. Leyla Kılıç Karakaynak opened it in 1996, and it has since spread across several shopfronts on the street.
places.address: Asmalı Mescit Mh., Kallavi Sk. No:13/1 (off İstiklal Cd.), 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Eleos
tips: A tasty rakı-balık (rakı and fish) on İstiklal. Not the cheapest, but some of the best fish I've ever eaten, and a stunning view onto the Bosphorus.
places.background: A Greek-leaning fish and meze restaurant for rakı-balık with a view, on the 2nd floor of the historic Hıdivyal Palas on İstiklal near Tünel, with blue-and-white decor and a terrace. It is known for fresh fish, grilled octopus and herb-heavy Turkish and Greek mezes. It is pricey for fish, which is charged at the daily market price. There is a separate, older branch in Yeşilköy.
places.address: Şahkulu Mh., İstiklal Cd. No:231, Hıdivyal Palas Kat 2, Beyoğlu (Tünel)/İstanbul

places.name: Tavanarası
places.background: A cosy, cramped attic restaurant on the 6th floor of Emre Han off Asmalı Mescit, reached by a rickety lift, with wooden decor and tightly packed tables. It is popular with locals; you write your order on paper. It is known for güveç (casseroles), meze, mücver and grilled fish, and serves alcohol.
places.address: Asmalı Mescit Cd. No:10 Kat 6 (Emre Han), 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Yeni Lokanta
places.pp: ₺7,800 tasting menu (+₺3,750 for 5-glass wine pairing); set menu ₺6,500
places.background: Chef Civan Er's modern Turkish restaurant on Kumbaracı Yokuşu, a bright room off İstiklal with à la carte or a tasting menu. The cooking is lighter and vegetable-forward, built on local produce, with an all-Turkish wine list. It has been open since at least 2013, and is listed in the MICHELIN Guide and on World's 50 Best Discovery.
places.address: Kumbaracı Yokuşu No:66/B, Şahkulu, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Aheste
tips: Slightly more upmarket: a delicious modern take on traditional Turkish food. You sit in a cosy candlelit alcove in the historic Pera district. Service is top notch and the wine list is fabulous.
My friend James says this is the best restaurant in Istanbul.
places.background: An intimate modern-Turkish meze and tasting-menu restaurant in Pera, upmarket but not stuffy, with a bistro area and a vaulted, candlelit dining room. The menu mixes traditional dishes (grilled lamb heart, kokoreç, dudi pilavı) with modern mezes, with good vegetarian options. It is listed in the MICHELIN Guide Istanbul.
places.address: Asmalı Mescit Mah., Meşrutiyet Cad. No:107/F, 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Galaktion
tips: Georgian, very traditional. Everything is delicious; the standard order for two is the Georgian salad, beef khinkali, Adjaruli khachapuri and chakhokhbili (tomato chicken stew).
It is *compulsory* to wash it down with a shot of chacha, a very strong Georgian spirit.
places.background: A homely Georgian kitchen with generous portions of khinkali, adjaruli khachapuri, chakhokhbili and other stews, plus Georgian wines, served in a book-filled room on Şehbender Sokak in Asmalımescit. Founded by Irakli Kakabadze and named after the poet Galaktion Tabidze, it began in a small storefront in Galata and moved near Taksim before settling here.
places.address: Asmalı Mescit Mah., Şehbender Sk., 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Petra Roasting Co. (Şişhane)
places.background: Petra's coffee-and-bakery café on the ground floor of the Bilsar building, on your left as you exit Şişhane metro. Petra calls it its newest café, and it is the closest Petra to Galata, Cihangir and Pera.
places.address: Evliya Çelebi, Meşrutiyet Cd. No:90/A, 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul (ground floor of the Bilsar building)

places.name: Hazzo Pulo (Passage Hazzopulo)
places.background: Hazzopulo Pasajı is a 19th-century passage between İstiklal and Meşrutiyet with a courtyard of tea houses and cafés. The wine stop inside is Hazzo Pulo (Meşrutiyet Cd. 31B), a small wine house and restaurant with a list of Turkish wines, which gives the passage its name in guidebooks.
places.address: Evliya Çelebi Mah., Meşrutiyet Cd. No:31B (Hazzopulo Pasajı), Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Varuna Gezgin Cafe
places.background: A multi-floor, traveller-themed café-bar with a terrace overlooking the Bosphorus, serving breakfast by day and fairly cheap drinks by night. It is the Istanbul branch of the Varuna Gezgin chain, founded by a teacher to promote backpacking, and has a 'Bahçe' branch at No:77.
places.address: Şahkulu, Kumbaracı Ykş. No:79/D (İstiklal Cd. entrance, Tünel), 34421 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

photos.credit: Photo: varunagezgin.com

places.name: Sensus Wine Boutique
places.background: An underground wine shop and tasting bar at the foot of Galata Tower for trying Turkish wines (sources cite 350–400+ labels) with cheese and charcuterie platters. Seating is limited.
places.address: Kuledibi, Bereketzade, Büyük Hendek Cd. No:5, 34420 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Okra İstanbul
places.background: An upscale restaurant with a bar on the 20th floor of The Marmara Taksim, with floor-to-ceiling views from the Bosphorus to the historic peninsula; go for a sunset cocktail at the bar or a full dinner. It opened around 2023 with a seasonal, open-fire Mediterranean/Turkish menu, cocktails and Turkish wines, and the bar section was added later. It is listed in the Michelin Guide (₺₺₺).
places.address: Gümüşsuyu, Osmanlı Sk. No:1/B, 34437 Beyoğlu/İstanbul (The Marmara Taksim, 20th floor)

places.name: Büyük Londra Hotel terrace bar
places.warning: The terrace bar is reported to open in the warm season only; it may be closed from late October. Check before going.
tips: Chill and not so expensive. Go at sunset, in time for the call to prayer echoing over the mosque-filled skyline.
places.background: A low-key, not-too-expensive seasonal hotel rooftop for a sunset drink over the Golden Horn and the old city, with a simple menu. It belongs to the Büyük Londra, an 1892 hotel built for Orient Express passengers and known for its eccentric antique lobby.
places.address: Asmalı Mescit Mh, Meşrutiyet Cd. No:53, 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Mikla bar
tips: The bar of this exclusive restaurant is open to everyone without a reservation. Probably the best view of Istanbul.
A small terrace in winter, still really worth it; in summer the top floor becomes a whole bar. A bit fancier than the others.
places.background: A fancy roof-terrace bar on top of The Marmara Pera, with panoramic views over the Golden Horn, the old city and the Bosphorus, and cocktails priced accordingly; it is open until 02:00. It belongs to Mikla, chef Mehmet Gürs's New Anatolian restaurant, listed among the World's 50 Best Restaurants (2022).
places.address: Asmalı Mescit, The Marmara Pera, Meşrutiyet Cd. No:15, 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Balkon
places.warning: Check the bill: a July 2026 Yandex review says staff once tried to add a ₺300 service charge and removed it only after the guest objected.
places.background: A casual, mid-priced rooftop restaurant-bar on the 6th floor of a building on Şehbender Sokak, with a big view over Tünel, the Golden Horn and the historic peninsula, easier on the wallet than the hotel rooftops nearby. It serves pub-style food (burgers, pizza, salads) and a long cocktail and wine list, and the evening programme moves to dance music. It has been running since 2004.
places.address: Asmalı Mescit, Şehbender Sk. No:5 D:M (6th floor), 34430 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Monkey Istanbul
tips: More electronic music, leaning towards techno.
places.background: A sunset-to-late cocktail rooftop on the 7th floor of the İKSV (Istanbul Foundation for Culture and Arts) building in Şişhane, with a wooden terrace over the Golden Horn and the historic peninsula. It serves signature cocktails and snacks while resident and guest DJs play laid-back house and disco (Time Out).
places.address: Nejat Eczacıbaşı Binası (İKSV), Sadi Konuralp Cd. No:5, 7th floor, Şişhane, 34433 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Gizli Bahçe
places.background: A packed, scruffy two-floor bar hidden among the meyhanes of Nevizade Sokak that turns into a dance floor late, with resident DJs playing alternative and electronic music. It is long-running, known as an LGBTQ-friendly venue, and has eclectic, worn-in decor.
places.address: Hüseyinağa Mah., Nevizade Sk. No:15, 34435 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Şahika
places.background: A busy multi-storey Nevizade landmark: a pub at street level and lounge floors for drinks, and a rooftop bar/club with Golden Horn views hosting techno, bass and D&B parties late in the week, as well as concerts, exhibitions and panels. Küçük Meyhane has moved into the building.
places.address: Hüseyinağa Mah., Nevizade Sk. No:5, Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Tarlabaşı Pazarı
places.background: A sprawling Sunday street market running down the Tarlabaşı backstreets, selling produce, dairy, fish, kitchenware, clothes and baked goods.
places.address: Karpuz Sk. area, Bülbül Mah., Tarlabaşı, Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Galata Tower
tips: Definitely worth going up for the incredible view.
places.background: An iconic medieval stone tower with a 360° viewing balcony over the Golden Horn and the Bosphorus; expect queues. The Genoese built it in the 14th century as part of the Galata walls, and since its 2020 restoration it has been run as a museum by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism.
places.address: Bereketzade Mah., Galata Kulesi, Beyoğlu, İstanbul

photos.credit: Photo: Juraj Patekar · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: BWV784 · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Karaköy
tips: 10 min walk from Cihangir, down the hill by the water. A few ivy-filled gorgeous streets to wander around. Grab a drink at any bar that catches your eye.
places.background: A waterfront district of cafés and bars in restored warehouses and ivy-covered lanes, at the Beyoğlu end of the Galata Bridge. The old port and banking district has filled with cafés, bars and galleries since the 2010s, and ferries leave from Karaköy pier.

photos.credit: Photo: Metuboy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Arild Vågen · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Dosseman · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Karaköy Çorba Evi
tips: Soups. You can ask for a ½ portion as a first course, then go on to the fish restaurant.
places.background: A cheap soup house on Mumhane Caddesi with about 20 soups, from mercimek and ezogelin to işkembe and kelle paça; order a half portion as a starter before a fish dinner. It started in 2011 as a soup-and-stew place and has traded as Karaköy Çorba Evi since 2014. Its website also mentions a Kadıköy location.
places.address: Kemankeş Karamustafa Paşa Mah., Mumhane Cd. No:35/A, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Can Balık (fish wrap, Karaköy)
tips: Balık dürüm: fish wrap.
places.background: One of the small balık-dürüm stalls on Fermeneciler Caddesi by the Karaköy fish market, near the Galata Bridge, for a quick grilled-fish wrap.
places.address: Arap Cami Mah., Fermeneciler Cd. No:30/A, 34010 Beyoğlu/İstanbul (Azapkapı)

places.name: Karaköy Lokantası
places.background: A smart, good-value harbourside restaurant with a tiled interior that works as a lokanta at lunch and a meze-and-rakı spot in the evening. It serves Turkish and Mediterranean meze, shared plates and traditional dishes with subtle Greek influences; the taramasalata and beef börek are highlights. It is listed in the Michelin Guide (₺₺).
places.address: Kemankeş Mh., Kemankeş Cd. No:57, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Mahkeme Lokantası
places.background: A tradesmen's lunch lokanta by day that becomes a lively classic meyhane at night, with crowds spilling onto the street. It is known for Girit ezme, pastırmalı humus, paçanga böreği and grilled octopus. It is housed in the historic Yoğurtçu Han, with a well-kept brick interior, and is named after the old Genoese courthouse across the street.
places.address: Azapkapı, Perşembe Pazarı Cd. No:14 (Yoğurtçu Han), 34421 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Arada Café
tips: Gorgeous Syrian/Lebanese restaurant in Tophane. Go for the huge Syrian breakfast: similar to the Turkish style, with more delicious dips.
places.background: A very popular all-day Lebanese-Syrian café-restaurant between Galata and Tophane; go for the huge Middle-Eastern breakfast, which adds hummus, fatteh, labneh with za'atar and falafel to the Turkish kahvaltı. It also serves mezes and grills all day. A pricier sister venue, Arada Endülüs, is about 60 m away at Kemeraltı Cd. 31.
places.address: Hacımimi Mah., Lüleci Hendek Cd. No:23A, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Karaköy Gümrük
places.background: An all-day restaurant in Karaköy's former customs-directorate building that turns into a cosy bar in the evening, with a modern-Turkish/Mediterranean kitchen, rakı, Turkish wine and cocktails. Reviewers like the interior, the dumplings and the cocktails; the upstairs bar has dark tones and black-and-white photos for a vintage feel. The building was reportedly restored and opened as Karaköy Gümrük in 2014.
places.address: Kemankeş Karamustafa Paşa, Gümrük Sk. No:4, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Nacht İstanbul
places.warning: Only one Resident Advisor night so far in 2026 and the website says 'coming soon'. Check RA before going.
places.background: A small house and minimal club on a Karaköy street (capacity 350) with a red, baroque-meets-modern interior, specialising in house, minimal house and groovy beats and booking DJs including Kater Blau (Berlin) regulars. Programming looks sporadic since mid-2025.
places.address: Kemankeş Mah., Mumhane Cd. No:52, 34425 Beyoğlu/İstanbul (Karaköy)

places.name: Kılıç Ali Paşa Hamamı
tips: The more expensive but stunning option, in Karaköy.
places.background: A high-end, strictly single-sex hamam: women 08:00–16:00, men in the evening. The Traditional Hamam Ritual (₺4,700) means resting on the heated marble platform, a kese scrub by an attendant and a foam wash at the basins; massages are extra (50-minute full body ₺5,000, 25-minute partial ₺3,800). Mimar Sinan built it in 1578–1583 for admiral Kılıç Ali Pasha to serve the Tophane mariners, its 14 m dome is the second largest of any Istanbul hamam, and it reopened after a long restoration.
places.address: Kemankeş Mah., Hamam Sk. No:1, 34425 Tophane, Karaköy, Beyoğlu/İstanbul

photos.credit: Photo: Metuboy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Metuboy · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Takeaway · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: R Prazeres · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Beşiktaş
tips: For football and pub vibes.
places.background: A lively, local, football-mad district on the European side of the Bosphorus, home of Beşiktaş JK and its Tüpraş Stadium; busy on match days. The çarşı (market area) behind the ferry pier is packed with cheap pubs, meyhanes and student bars.

photos.credit: Photo: Chapultepec · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Istanbulensis · Public domain · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: No machine-readable author provided. Bertilvidet~commonswiki · CC BY 2.5 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Ali Ocakbaşı Gümüşsuyu
tips: Kebab and Turkish food, with a Bosphorus view.
places.background: An upscale ocakbaşı on İnönü Caddesi with a Bosphorus view and a polished take on kebab and meze: charcoal kebabs, lahmacun, and mezes such as muhammara and Girit ezme. It is the Gümüşsuyu branch of a grill house group with branches in Karaköy, Suadiye, Amsterdam and Barcelona, which promotes zero-waste, sustainable sourcing.
places.address: Gümüşsuyu, İnönü Cd. No:22, 34870 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Petra Roasting Co. (Gayrettepe)
places.background: Petra's headquarters café and roastery in the Gayrettepe business district, the original Petra. Go if you are nearby; it is not worth a detour for visitors.
places.address: Gayrettepe, Hoşsohbet Sk. (Selenium residence), Beşiktaş/İstanbul

places.name: Setup
tips: My favourite bar in the area. Bosphorus view and good food. You might need a reservation at the weekend.
places.background: A neighbourhood café-bar on the Kabataş Setüstü strip above the ferry pier, with a Bosphorus view, serving breakfast through dinner and cocktails to quiet jazz. It has been renovated. Sister venues Setup Burger and Deli Meyhane are a few doors down İnebolu Sokak.
places.address: Ömer Avni Mah., İnebolu Sk. No:9/15, Setüstü Kabataş, 34427 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Kaiser Kabataş
places.background: A friendly small bar and gastropub on İnebolu Sokak on the Setüstü strip near the Kabataş ferry stop, with outdoor seating facing the Bosphorus. It serves burgers, bowls, breakfast and cocktails. It is rated 4.9 from 201 reviews on TripAdvisor and was a 2026 Travellers' Choice.
places.address: Ömer Avni, İnebolu Sk. No:31/A, Kabataş Setüstü, 34427 Beyoğlu/İstanbul

places.name: Beşiktaş Pazarı
places.background: A big weekly neighbourhood market for produce and household goods.
places.address: Nüzhetiye Cd., Muradiye/Teşvikiye side, Beşiktaş/İstanbul

places.name: Avokado Bar
tips: Healthy food: vegan, vegetarian and more.
places.background: A healthy all-day café and specialty-coffee bar in Teşvikiye, Nişantaşı, for brunch or lunch: avocado tartines on sourdough, grain bowls (quinoa patties, salmon), smoothies and smoothie bowls, and refined-sugar-free desserts, with many vegan, vegetarian and gluten-free options. Despite the 'bar' name, there is no alcohol on the menu.
places.address: Teşvikiye, Ahmet Fetgari Sk. No:29/B, 34365 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: TURK Fatih Tutak
places.background: Chef Fatih Tutak's tasting-menu restaurant in Bomonti, a top-tier experience lasting about three hours; book weeks ahead. A single menu of about 12–14 courses built on Turkish regional produce is served across a city-view lounge, a dining room facing the kitchen and, for dessert, the open kitchen, with a strong Turkish wine list. It won two MICHELIN stars in the first Istanbul guide (October 2022) and is still listed with two.
places.address: Cumhuriyet Mah., Hacıahmet Silahşör Cad., Yeniyol Sk. No:2, 34440 Şişli/İstanbul (Bomonti)

places.name: Seorabeol Korean Restaurant
places.background: A proper, long-running Korean restaurant in the business district, serving Istanbul's Korean community, and pricier than average. It is known for free banchan refills, yukgaejang and Korean fried chicken.
places.address: Raşit Rıza Sk. No:3, Mecidiyeköy, 34847 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Spada Coffee (Nişantaşı)
places.background: A small, self-service specialty coffee bar of Spada Roastery on a quiet Teşvikiye side street, with about 10 tables indoors and out. It serves espresso drinks, pour-overs of its own beans, Japanese matcha, house-made cold teas and refined-sugar-free bakes. It has been here since 2016; Spada also has a branch in Fişekhane and a roastery in Bakırköy.
places.address: Teşvikiye, Av. Süreyya Ağaoğlu Sk. No:8/E, 34365 Şişli/İstanbul

photos.credit: Photo: spadacoffee.com

places.name: Petra Roasting Co. (Topağacı)
places.warning: OpenStreetMap labels this address 'Kronotrop Topağacı', while Petra's 2026 site still lists the café. Check before going.
places.background: Petra's sit-down neighbourhood café in historic Topağacı, Nişantaşı, with table service and a bar-food menu as well as coffee. Petra describes it as a real mahalle coffee house with a 1930s-inspired interior. Petra Roasting Co. is one of Istanbul's early specialty roasters, with its HQ and roastery in Gayrettepe.
places.address: Teşvikiye, Prof. Dr. Orhan Ersek Sk. 18/7, 34365 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Coffee Department Nişantaşı
places.background: The Nişantaşı branch of Coffee Department, an Istanbul specialty roaster that also has a café in Balat, on a quiet Teşvikiye side street. A spot for a coffee break, with desserts.
places.address: Teşvikiye, Sezai Selek Sk. No:28/30-B, 34365 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Montag Coffee Bomonti
places.background: The Bomonti branch of Montag Coffee, the Kadıköy specialty roaster (see Montag Coffee Moda), on Silahşör Caddesi. Google lists it as a coffee shop and roastery.
places.address: Cumhuriyet, Silahşör Cd. No:65/B, 34380 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Dekk
places.warning: Dekk's own site now lists only its Akmerkez location (opened Oct 2025); this Maçka terrace may have closed. Check before going.
places.background: An open-air 2,500 m² food hall and cocktail bar (dekkBar) on the terrace of the Lütfi Kırdar Congress Centre near Maçka Park, with street-food stalls, concerts and workshops; best in good weather. It opened in autumn 2021, and a second, indoor-outdoor dekk opened in Akmerkez on 11 October 2025.
places.address: Harbiye, Darülbedai Cd. No:4 (Lütfi Kırdar Congress Centre terrace), 34367 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Joker No.5
places.background: A buzzing, popular bar-restaurant on Atiye Sokak in Nişantaşı with indoor seating and street tables, drawing locals and visitors. It is known for cocktails such as piña colada and daiquiri, and bar food like mini burgers.
places.address: Harbiye, Atiye Sk. No:5, 34367 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Efendi Topağacı
places.background: A small, hole-in-the-wall street-side cocktail bar in Topağacı that spills onto the street and gets crowded on weekends. It is run by a mixologist known as 'Dede', with signature cocktails, a mostly local crowd, and funk and soul music.
places.address: Teşvikiye, Hacı Emin Efendi Sk. No:28(/A), 34365 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Karloff
places.background: A dim, moody, speakeasy-style cocktail bar on Topağacı's bar street in Nişantaşı, the same street as Efendi. It serves cocktails, whisky and a few beers, with groovy music and a pool table.
places.address: Teşvikiye, Hacı Emin Efendi Sk. No:41, 34365 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Blok Cafe Mekan
places.background: A big multi-space Bomonti venue on Silahşör Caddesi with two bars, a live-music area, an exhibition space upstairs and an open roof area at the back. It is open from midday into the night.
places.address: Cumhuriyet Mah., Silahşör Cd. No:65 (65/B–D), 34380 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Bosphorus Brewing Company
places.background: An English-Turkish brewpub near Gayrettepe metro in the business district, with a terrace and beer brewed on site; it is one of the few places in Istanbul pouring its own draught craft beer, with Istanbul Pale Ale as the flagship and a reported 12 house taps. The food is British gastropub style (ploughman's, bangers and mash, fish and chips). Its website says it has hosted guests for over 14 years.
places.address: Esentepe, Yıldız Posta Cd. No:1 D:1A, 34394 Şişli/İstanbul

places.name: Feriköy Pazarı
places.background: A covered market hall in Bomonti that hosts the well-known Feriköy antique and flea market.
places.address: Gökkuşağı Sk. No:6, Cumhuriyet Mah., Şişli/İstanbul (Bomonti/Feriköy)

places.name: Arnavutköy
tips: A beautiful part of Istanbul on the water. Lovely to walk around. Get brunch at A Bit of Eggo, an afternoon beer at Hide Arnavutköy, and vegan food at Gabfoods. You can walk or scooter up along the water to Bebek and beyond, e.g. to Emirgan.
places.background: A pretty Bosphorus village of wooden Ottoman houses in Beşiktaş district, between Kuruçeşme and Bebek. A seafront walking and cycling path runs along the water north to Bebek and beyond, making it good for a stroll.

photos.credit: Photo: büys · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Maestroka at English Wikipedia · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Yaguzi · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Ömer Ünlü · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: A Bit of Eggo
tips: Brunch in Arnavutköy.
places.background: An egg-focused café on a quiet Arnavutköy back street, serving breakfast all day: menemen, frittata and an 'Egg'on Kruvasan' croissant with poached egg, plus layered crêpe desserts. There is a tree-shaded outdoor area.
places.address: Abdülhak Molla Sk. No:26, Arnavutköy, 34345 Beşiktaş/İstanbul

places.name: MSA'nın Restoranı (Sakıp Sabancı Museum)
places.pp: ₺2,500–4,000 for a main + drink (derived from menu)
places.background: A smart restaurant with a Bosphorus-view terrace in the Sakıp Sabancı Museum, run as the training restaurant of Mutfak Sanatları Akademisi (MSA, Istanbul Culinary Arts Academy): students cook and serve under professional chefs. The food is strong, mixing world cuisines with seasonal Turkish produce, though service can be patchy. It opened around 2017 in the space formerly occupied by Müzedechanga and is open to the public without a museum ticket.
places.address: Emirgan Mah., Sakıp Sabancı Cd. No:42, 34467 Sarıyer/İstanbul (inside Sakıp Sabancı Museum)

places.name: Petra Roasting Co. (Bebek)
places.background: A garden café on a Bebek back street, a nice coffee stop on a Bosphorus walk. Petra describes it as an old neighbourhood coffee house in a grandmother's-house-style garden, with the full menu, a General Store corner and the freshest beans.
places.address: Bebek Mah., Küçükbebek Cd. (near No. 38), Beşiktaş/İstanbul

places.name: Petra Roasting Co. (Maslak)
places.background: A Petra coffee corner inside the MUDO Concept store in the Maslak business district. Not a visitor destination.
places.address: MUDO Concept, Maslak Mah., Eski Büyükdere Cd. No:7, Sarıyer/İstanbul

places.name: Dirty Hands
places.background: A loud neighbourhood street-food bar in Akatlar serving fried kokoreç bites, bao, tacos, wraps and Tex-Mex burgers with cocktails and tequila shots. After 23:00 the tables are cleared and it turns into a small club. It comes from the team behind Arnavutköy's 'Any'.
places.address: Akat, Zeytinoğlu Cd. No:7, 34335 Beşiktaş/İstanbul

places.name: Hide Arnavutköy
tips: An afternoon beer in Arnavutköy.
places.background: A café-restaurant in a large, leafy hidden garden courtyard off Arnavutköy's back streets, for brunch or an afternoon drink; pricier than its neighbours. The seasonal, French/American-leaning menu is built around breakfast and lunch, with bakery items, desserts, freshly ground coffee and vegan and gluten-free options.
places.address: Arnavutköy, Dere Sk. No:8, 34345 Beşiktaş/İstanbul

places.name: All Sports Cafe
places.background: A long-running Etiler neighbourhood café-restaurant decorated with sports memorabilia, more café than bar, serving bowls and desserts. There is a fixed menu plus a rotating daily menu and a small summer garden. A regular says it has been around for 25 years, and there is also a Nişantaşı branch.
places.address: Etiler, Bıyıklı Mehmet Paşa Sk. No:1 D:2, 34337 Beşiktaş/İstanbul

places.name: Taps Bebek
places.background: A relaxed, busy waterfront brewpub in a three-storey house on the Bosphorus shore, with Bosphorus and marina views. It brews its own beers (red ale, strong ale, kölsch, rotating drafts) and serves burgers and international pub food. Taps started in Nişantaşı in 2002 and has been in Bebek since 2008.
places.address: Bebek, Cevdetpaşa Cd. No:119, 34342 Beşiktaş/İstanbul

places.name: Sakıp Sabancı Museum (Emirgan)
places.pp: ₺450 adult ticket (₺330 discounted, ₺225 student; free on Tuesdays)
tips: Beautiful museum gardens. The museum has a fixed collection as well as changing exhibitions.
places.background: Sabancı University's art museum in the 'Atlı Köşk', a former Sabancı family mansion on the Bosphorus in Emirgan, with terraced gardens overlooking the water. It holds a permanent collection of Ottoman calligraphy and paintings and hosts big temporary international exhibitions.
places.address: Sakıp Sabancı Cd. No:42, Emirgan, 34467 Sarıyer/İstanbul

photos.credit: Photo: Edal · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Bant ist (talk) · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Edal Anton Lefterov · CC BY-SA 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: mikail dağlı · CC BY 3.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Balat
places.background: A colourful historic quarter on the Golden Horn in Fatih, with photogenic steep streets, churches and synagogues, and a growing café and antiques scene. It was traditionally home to Jewish, Greek and Armenian communities.

photos.credit: Photo: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Antoloji · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Mondo79 from Freiburg im Breisgau, Germany · CC BY 2.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: Antoloji · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: Moda
tips: On the Asian side; it has recently stolen the crown from Cihangir as the 'trendiest' place in Istanbul. You can get anything here, including Portuguese custard tarts, Japanese mochi and Vietnamese pho.
Best part: hanging out on the rocks along the waterfront for a sunset beer. Getting there means taking the ferry across the Bosphorus, another key part of Istanbul.
places.background: A trendy neighbourhood on a small peninsula in Kadıköy on the Asian side, a short walk from Kadıköy ferry pier. It is known for its cafés and bars, the Moda Sahili seafront park, and the rocky shoreline where people gather at sunset.

photos.credit: Photo: Vikimedyahesap · CC BY-SA 4.0 · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons
Photo: A.Savin · FAL · Wikimedia Commons

places.name: 700 Gram
tips: The tastiest eggs Benedict (Moda).
places.background: A small neighbourhood breakfast and brunch café in Moda, with eggs Benedict variants on the menu, including salmon Benedict. Time Out reviewed it in 2015, describing breakfast plates with three cheeses, olives, buffalo cream and homemade jam, filling toasts, and eggs and greens from the owners' garden in Yakacık.
places.address: Caferağa Mah., Ruşen Ağa Sk. No:3/C, Moda, 34710 Kadıköy/İstanbul

places.name: Çiya Sofrası
tips: Turkish food on the Asian side.
places.background: A canteen-style counter of rotating regional dishes in the Kadıköy market; go at lunch for the widest choice. Musa Dağdeviren's restaurant grew out of a modest kebab shop and researches and revives regional Anatolian, Mesopotamian and Caucasian recipes. It was featured in Netflix's Chef's Table (vol. 5) and ranked on Opinionated About Dining's Casual Europe list in 2024 and 2025.
places.address: Caferağa, Güneşlibahçe Sk. No:43, 34710 Kadıköy/İstanbul

places.name: Viktor Levi Şarap Evi
tips: A beautiful garden to enjoy a long evening dinner with friends (Moda).
places.background: A big, lively wine house in Moda with a large courtyard garden for long dinners with friends, where the wine matters more than the food. It pours house wines such as Papaz Karası and Ada Karası and fruit wines, with a bistro menu of grills, pasta and cheese plates. It descends from the historic Viktor Levi wine shop in Beyoğlu, reportedly founded in 1914; the Beyoğlu venue has closed.
places.address: Caferağa Mh., Moda Cd., Damacı Sk. No:4, Kadıköy/İstanbul (behind Reks Cinema)

places.name: Story Coffee & Food
places.background: The Moda flagship café of Story Coffee Roasters, who roast their own coffee in Istanbul, in a historic house with a garden; good for coffee and brunch (burritos, pancakes). Story also has cafés in Yeldeğirmeni (Halitağa Cad. 61) and Tepe Nautilus mall.
places.address: Caferağa Mah., Dalga Sk. No:22, Moda, Kadıköy/İstanbul

places.name: Montag Coffee (Moda)
places.background: The Moda branch of Montag Coffee, a Kadıköy specialty roaster, on a back street steps from Story. Montag roasts its own beans, has cafés in Kadıköy (Muvakkithane Cad.), Moda and Bomonti, and is credited with bringing third-wave coffee to Kadıköy in the mid-2010s (2014 or 2015; sources differ).
places.address: Caferağa Mah. Bademaltı Sok. No:22/A, Moda, Kadıköy/İstanbul
